newsitem.title: FRANCE: Belgian Renault workers clash with French police.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Renault workers clash with French police.

text.p: Striking Belgian Renault workers clashed with French police on Thursday outside a compound in northern France where thousands of cars are stored, witnesses said.

Para-military gendarmes protecting the site at Wavrin, south of the city of Lille, fired tear gas after being stoned by some 400 workers from the Renault plant at Vilvoorde in the Brussels suburbs, due to be closed in July with the loss of 3,100 jobs.

Police reinforcements were brought in to disperse the strikers, who drove to France by bus to carry out surprise actions against Renault after company chairman Louis Schweitzer told their union representatives on Wednesday that the decision to close the Vilvoorde assembly plant was irrevocable.

In Paris, about 100 Renault workers demonstrated outside the company's headquarters in the suburb of Boulogne-Billancourt. Police turned away a group of workers who tried to enter the company's prestige showroom on the Champs-Elysees avenue.
In Wavrin, gendarmerie captain Alain Salort said his men had reached an agreement with the protesters that police would leave the depot if the demonstrators promised not to damage the 9,000 cars.

Belgian metalworkers' union official Herwig Jorissen told reporters: "We are going to stay the weekend or a whole week if necessary. We want the keys to the cars to prevent Renault from resupplying its dealers."
The clash occurred hours before Renault, the smallest of Europe's six carmakers, was expected to announce a heavy loss in 1996, which Schweitzer says makes restructuring essential.
Union officials say Renault has increased the number of cars stocked at Wavrin to resupply its Belgian dealerships once supplies of cars from Vilvoorde are exhausted.
Workers have been occupying the plant there since February 27, when Renault announced the closure plan, and have taken hostage the cars stocked at the factory.
